propositions: Push recovery's _recover_dirty_merge fails permanently when untracked local files collide with files the remote merge wants to create (e.g. compaction leftovers like *-SNAPSHOT.json, *.retired), because merge aborts and the recovery path gives up without self-healing.
The same untracked-overwrite collision class already has a proven recovery in sync.py's reconverge path using untracked file quarantine; push recovery must reuse that shape.
After merge abort due to untracked collision, quarantine the named colliding paths to the shared directory structure, retry the merge once, and restore the stash exactly once on all exit paths.

The recovery parser is imported from sync._untracked_overwrite_paths (pure, no subprocess), but the mover runs through the local push_recovery seam (core._git) to preserve ~25 existing test monkeypatch sites.
Genuine content conflicts and unnamed paths must retain today's abort-restore-warn behavior unchanged; the quarantine move and single retry apply only when git names untracked-overwrite collisions.
